title: Integration discovery - Lumina Health & Redwood

Agreed next steps include sharing security pack, pricing for dedicated pools, and scheduling a POC/benchmark run with sample traffic.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2028-01-15
Time: 15:00 - 15:48 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Sara Patel (Lumina CTO), Evan Brooks (Platform Lead), Priya Menon (Secops), Jordan Lee (ML Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Quick discovery focusing on integration options. Customer leaning toward Dedicated or Private due to PHI/data residency; exploring LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters and gateway approach.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, im maya from Redwood, joining today is diego our se. quick roll call?
[00:00:08] Sara (Lumina CTO): hey this is sara, evan, priya and jordan here as well.
[00:00:12] Diego (Redwood SE): good to meet you all. quick agenda: understand your current stack, integration points, and success criteria for a POC.
[00:00:22] Evan (Lumina): sounds good. high level: we run most services in gcp, some workloads on prem (sensitive patient pipelines). currently using OpenAI for prototypes but moving to in-house inference for PHI. primary concern is latency and auditability.
[00:00:40] Maya: got it. so main buckets today: 1) which deployment (hosted/dedicated/private) makes sense, 2) SDK and langchain support, 3) gateway/proxy and rate-limit patterns, 4) observability hooks for tracing and cost.
[00:00:55] Priya (Lumina SecOps): quick note — we need SOC2 and KMS integration. If you have a private/VPC option that's interesting. Also SSO for admin console.
[00:01:05] Diego: yes we support private deployments with VPC and customer-managed keys; our private plane — sorry private control plane — integrates with KMS, HSMs in many cases. (small stutter) we can share our security pack.
[00:01:20] Jordan (ML Eng): on the SDK side, we use LangChain and LlamaIndex for retrieval-augmented generation. do you have direct adapters?
[00:01:30] Diego: we have official SDKs in python/node and community adapters for LangChain. for LlamaIndex there's a community connector; SEs have run quickstarts. we'll share example repos. note: some adapter names in docs are slightly different, the auto-docs sometimes say redwood-client vs redwood-sdk.
[00:01:50] Sara: great. for the POC we want to validate three things: latency under 150ms p50 for short prompts, cost per 1k tokens, and end-to-end audit logs for each request.
[00:02:04] Maya: good crisp criteria. what volume are you expecting?
[00:02:10] Evan: baseline 50 qps with bursts to 250 qps during peak times. most requests are short - 50-120 tokens. some longer transcripts occasionally.
[00:02:22] Diego: that matches one of our typical profiles. dedicated pools with autoscale can hit that; dedicated gives you predictable throughput and isolation. hosted could work for early stages but for PHI and compliance you'd likely look at dedicated or private.
[00:02:38] Priya: clarify private vs dedicated — private means our control plane is customer-managed?
[00:02:44] Diego: Private means you get a private control plane and the option for on-prem inference; dedicated is Redwood-managed reserved GPU pools with isolated capacity but control plane still hosted by Redwood.
[00:02:56] Priya: ok thanks.
[00:03:00] [00:03:00] Maya: on the integration patterns, you mentioned gateway/proxy — can you describe your current architecture?
[00:03:08] Evan: we have an API gateway (gke) and an internal model proxy that fans out to different providers. we'd either put a Redwood gateway sidecar or call the Redwood SDK from our services. latency budget is tight so avoiding extra network hops preferred.
[00:03:26] Diego: two common approaches: 1) sidecar/proxy pattern — deploy a lightweight proxy near your app that routes to Redwood endpoint; 2) direct SDK calls from your service to Redwood with signed keys and gateway for rate-limiting. sidecar reduces round trips for local batching. both support quota/rate-limit headers.
[00:03:48] Jordan: does Redwood expose tokens-per-request or estimate in headers? we want to attribute cost per feature.
[00:03:55] Diego: yes we return token usage in response metadata and have per-route cost breakdown in the console and via observability hooks. we also provide trace ids you can propagate. sometimes auto-transcription shows the header as token-usage, docs might say usage_tokens.
[00:04:12] Priya: about rate limits: if we burst to 250 qps and then drop, how do you handle throttling and retries? we can't have user-visible failures.
[00:04:20] Diego: we support token-based quotas, rate-limit headers (x-rw-rl, x-rw-remaining) and client-side libraries include exponential backoff helpers. for dedicated pools we can configure burst capacity and reserved throughput to avoid 429s. also recommend local batching or prefix caching for repeated prompts.
[00:04:36] Sara: interested in KV caching — we do a lot of RAG where prefix caching would save cost. how does that work with Redwood caching?
[00:04:44] Diego: our runtime supports KV cache for model state and prefix cache for prompt fragments; in Hosted we do multi-tenant cache, in Dedicated you can have tenant-isolated caches which helps cost predictability. note: caching semantics depend on prompt uniqueness.
[00:04:59] Evan: on instrumentation — can we get spans into our tracing system (we use Datadog)?
[00:05:04] Diego: yes we emit trace headers and can push logs/metrics to your observability backend via exporters. the console also shows token-level latency and cost. we'll share docs for traces and an example of integrating with Datadog.
[00:05:16] Sara: timeline — we need something validated for a HIPAA-scoped pilot in Q1. is a 2-3 week POC realistic?
[00:05:24] Maya: yes a 1-2 week technical POC is doable if we get sample traffic and target SLAs. for HIPAA-scoped pilot we'll need a signed BAA and Private or Dedicated with customer-managed keys.
[00:05:36] Priya: BAA and SOC2 reports are must-haves. also want to confirm retention policies and audit log retention.
[00:05:42] Maya: we'll include retention options in the security pack. default logs retention 30 days, with enterprise add-on for longer.
[00:05:50] Jordan: about LangChain — how does the retry/backoff play with chain-of-thought prompts? if an intermediate step times out do you re-run the whole chain?
[00:05:58] Diego: good question; typical integration is to checkpoint intermediate outputs in your app layer (e.g., store embeddings or partial results). our SDK has helpers but we recommend application-level checkpoints to avoid recompute.
[00:06:12] Sara: competitors: we've tested OpenAI and Anthropic; Anthropic had slightly higher latency for some prompts, OpenAI good but costy. curious about Redwood cost model for Dedicated.
[00:06:24] Maya: dedicated pricing is primarily reserved capacity + per-token unit economics; we'll include a sample cost model based on your qps distribution.
[00:06:31] Evan: any hard limits on model size or quantization? we run some 70B models in our infra.
[00:06:36] Diego: runtime supports many quantized variants up to 70B-ish depending on instance types; for very large models we recommend dedicated GPU pools with specific hardware. we'll map model+hw recommendations in the POC plan.
[00:06:50] [00:06:50] Maya: quick demo note — we can provide a notebook that demonstrates SDK -> LangChain -> Redwood end-to-end with a sample RAG pipeline.
[00:06:58] Priya: about SSO — we use Okta; need SAML for the console and SCIM for provisioning.
[00:07:04] Diego: supported, we have SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. we'll include config examples.
[00:07:10] Evan: can you share a sample of observability hooks — specifically how traces correlate to tokens and cost?
[00:07:16] Diego: yes, the trace payload includes request_id, model, token_count, latency_ms and a cost_estimate field. exportable via our logs endpoint or via direct integration with your logging/metrics system.
[00:07:28] Jordan: any gotchas with LangChain memory or LlamaIndex connectors? sometimes connector callbacks expect synchronous responses.
[00:07:36] Diego: our SDK supports sync and async; however, some higher-level wrappers in community packages were written with slightly different assumptions. we'll include wrapper code to make it drop-in. note: docs sometimes reference an older API path (/v1/generate vs /v1/responses) so watch for that.
[00:07:52] Sara: ok this feels promising. next steps?
[00:07:56] Maya: recap: we'll send security pack (SOC2, BAA template, KMS integration notes), SE will share LangChain/LlamaIndex examples and notebook, and we'll propose a POC plan with pricing and recommended hardware. Lumina will share request distribution and compliance constraints.
[00:08:12] Evan: we'll aim to provide traffic shapes and a contact for legal by 2028-01-19.
[00:08:18] Priya: we'll review the security pack and confirm scope.
[00:08:22] Maya: cool, i'll put calendar invites for the POC planning session.
[00:08:26] Diego: any final tech questions?
[00:08:29] Jordan: curious if you support model rollouts/canary testing in Dedicated — like canary between quantized vs full-precision?
[00:08:36] Diego: yes, rollout controls are supported — canary, A/B, automatic fallback to cheaper variants on perf regressions. we can demo that in the POC.
[00:08:46] Sara: thanks all, we'll follow up after internal alignment.
[00:08:50] Maya: thanks everyone appreciate it.

[00:20:00] (mid-call deep dive)
[00:20:04] Diego: quick note on gateway/proxy patterns — the recommended pattern for low-latency RAG is sidecar with local batching and prefix caching; language clients call local proxy which keeps KV cache warm and reduces remote calls. we can share a Helm chart for that.
[00:20:28] Evan: that would be useful. do you support TLS mutual auth for the proxy->redwood connection?
[00:20:33] Diego: yes mTLS supported for Private deployments and for Dedicated we can enable client certs.
[00:20:40] Priya: what about observability retention for audit logs — 30 days default was mentioned, can be extended?
[00:20:46] Maya: yes enterprise add-on for longer retention and archived logs to your S3/GCS bucket.

[00:35:00] (closing)
[00:35:05] Maya: thanks all. i'll email the pack and deck after this. diego will send code samples. look forward to the POC.
[00:35:15] Sara: thanks, bye.

--- End transcript ---
